about: Differences between the port's hole-table escalation (src/hole_table.rs, native recognition) and draftwright's on the same parts (tests/fixtures/hole_tables.json), each with its verdict. Read by tests/hole_tables.rs.

ctc02.reason: Seven ⌀8.4 ↧25 holes are loose holes in the port's plan (quiddity-rust's native recognition puts them in no pattern) and so table rows; draftwright's table leaves them out, as it leaves out the members of recognised patterns (its Python quiddity recognition differs). Every row both tables have (22 holes: the eight ⌀10.1, the ⌀120, the six ⌀22, five ⌀8.4 and the two ⌀12) prints the same cells; the tags shift after the first difference. Which grouping is right is recognition's question (quiddity-rust), not the escalation's.

ctc04.reason: draftwright's model has four ⌀12 ↧20 and four ⌀10.1 ↧30 z holes at x 155 and 345 that the port's plan view calls out nowhere: quiddity-rust's native recognition does not give them as plan-view holes. The ten rows both have (the two ⌀12.1 ↧15 and eight ⌀14 THRU) print the same cells.

ctc02.reason: draftwright attempts a table on CTC-02 (and withdraws it for want of balloon room) because its placement drops seven plan-view hole callouts for settled ink crossing their text, and its ladders for crowding; the port drops only an item placed off the sheet (src/hole_table.rs, departures: rust-correct for now, the collisions placed and reported), and since the layout reserves every view's bands (drawing quality 3) none of CTC-02's is off the sheet, so it attempts none. Neither draws a table. The withdrawal itself is checked on CTC-02 with a stand-in drop (a_table_without_every_balloon_is_withdrawn_whole).

ctc04.reason: draftwright attempts a table (its plan view has 18 holes outside a pattern, at least 16) and withdraws it for want of balloon room; the port's has 10 (the eight holes above missing), fewer than 16, so it attempts none and says so on each drop. Neither draws a table. Follows the recognition difference in rows.ctc04.

plan_time_schedules.reason: Maintainer direction 2026-10-11: dense views use tables before layout, rather than escalating only after a dropped item. Python origin/main src/draftwright/annotations/orchestrator.py::_maybe_tabulate_holes_impl retains the >=16 loose-hole rescue and excludes compound/authored callouts from replacement. The Rust rescue is unchanged; the new presentation keeps full approved compound/thread/fit/tolerance wording in a size cell, per-hole coordinate cells, compact tags and a proven projected datum corner. Pinned callouts are additive. Ordinary PCD notes are retained. Tests: planned_hole_tables.rs; original failure logs and native before/after sheets under target/h1-*. H1 fix round: use a theoretical min-plane corner (Python orchestrator.py:1718-1719 also specifies a min-corner datum), entry coordinates/directions distinguish stacked openings, one shared tag identifies coaxial rows, and an incomplete concentric circle prints PCD with explicit angles. Model-space boundary and side-on bore evidence prevents new tag collisions; quality.py measures all schedule labels against actual SVG edges. Evidence: planned_hole_tables regressions and target/h1-fix-*.
plan_time_schedules.policy: Always requests the new complete schedule presentation; unpinned callouts may be replaced. This deliberately differs from Python's additive public hole-table verb. A requested schedule without a provable datum or clear space warns and keeps the complete original drawing.
